html:
SMTO-AUT-0019 — The saved Google app setup has a mistake

GUID: bb0f83e2-f3f8-5fb6-97bc-a1d674076841
Slug: google-oauth-app-invalid
Domain: AUT · Subsystem: google-workspace

What happened

  • The Google app setup SMTO was told to use is either the wrong kind of entry or has settings SMTO can't accept. SMTO stopped before opening a Google sign-in, so nothing was connected or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Parameter Store (from the More options ⋯ menu), make sure the name you gave SMTO is the Google app entry, not one described as “Google Workspace authorization for” an email. Those are connected-account entries; SMTO stops if the name points to the wrong kind of entry, even a valid one.
  2. Ask the person who manages SMTO to compare the entry with a fresh Google Workspace OAuth App template, keeping Google's sign-in addresses unchanged and removing any extra fields. SMTO only accepts Google's own sign-in addresses and the fields that template provides.
  3. If the app type is web, they must add the client secret and a return address ending in /api/agent/google/oauth/callback. A desktop app leaves that address empty. Google sends you back to that exact address after sign-in, so a wrong or missing one would break the connection.
  4. When the entry is fixed, ask SMTO to connect your Google account again using that entry. SMTO checks the entry again each time it starts a Google sign-in.

What success looks like

  • SMTO gives you a Google sign-in link, and after you finish, the page says your email is connected and you can close the window.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the client secret into the conversation, and don't edit a connected Google account entry to work around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google OAuth application validation failed: the record at the key is not a google_oauth_app, or it has unknown or missing fields, an unsupported version or feature, changed Google endpoints, or an inconsistent client type and redirect URI.

What this means

  • The Google application profile has the wrong type, unsupported fields/version or inconsistent endpoint, feature and callback configuration. Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.

Why this can happen

  • The Google application profile has the wrong type, unsupported fields/version or inconsistent endpoint, feature and callback configuration.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the client type, fixed Google endpoints, requested feature scopes and callback with the application profile schema.

How to fix it

  • Check the google_oauth_app record against auth/google/profiles.py: profile_version 1, non-empty client_id, authorization_uri and token_uri equal to Google's pinned endpoints, only known requested_features, requested_scopes empty or exactly the features' scopes, and no extra fields. A desktop client must have an empty redirect_uri; a web client needs client_secret and a redirect_uri whose path is exactly /api/agent/google/oauth/callback with no query, matching the URI registered in Google Cloud Console.
  • Check the client type, Google endpoints, selected features and registered web callback in Parameter Store.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm account identity and required features before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended application profile passes validation with its registered callback and supported features.

What not to do

  • Do not expose client secrets, tokens, codes or PKCE verifiers.
  • Do not switch accounts or repeat uncertain mutations automatically.

Technical notes

  • Authorization establishes a particular connection, account and scope. It neither expands operation permissions nor proves the outcome of a request already dispatched.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
